priorStatuses.title: Remove the message listener during cleanup

findings.title: [P2] Restore socket listener removal
findings.body: The returned cleanup callback no longer removes the registered message handler. Consumers that dispose and reattach will retain old handlers, causing messages to be processed multiple times and retaining referenced state indefinitely.

findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the polling disposer
findings.body: Calling the returned cleanup function no longer stops the interval. In Node.js, even one disposed poller can keep the process alive indefinitely; repeated setup/cleanup cycles retain every `refresh` closure and execute all of them once per second, causing unbounded CPU and memory growth.

findings.title: [P2] Remove the message listener during cleanup
findings.body: This previously reported defect remains open after current-source revalidation. Evidence: Current src/socket.ts line 3 still returns an empty disposer after registering handler on line 2; the full diff shows this PR replaced socket.off("message", handler), so cleanup continues to retain and invoke the listener.
